findings.title: JSON-LD 5-schema bundle is correctly rendered as plain SSR <script> (NOT next/script) — the #1 GEO mistake is avoided
findings.detail: src/app/layout.tsx renders all 5 schemas in the SSR <head> via <StructuredData>: WebSite, Person, ProfessionalService (LocalBusiness), FAQPage (5 Q&A), and WebPage(dates). src/components/seo/structured-data.tsx emits a real <script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML=...> — plain tag, so it lands in the initial HTML where AI crawlers see it (the geo-aeo-protocol #1 rule). Bundle satisfies the WebSite+Person/Org+ProfessionalService+WebPage(dates)+FAQPage(>=5) requirement.

findings.title: hreflang "en" and canonical alternate point to /en, which has NO index page (404) — real GEO/SEO bug
findings.detail: Both src/app/layout.tsx (line 66) and src/app/page.tsx (line 17) declare alternates.languages['en'] = `${SITE_URL}/en`, and layout also emits <link rel="alternate" hrefLang=... >. But src/app/en/ contains only /en/claude-code, /en/guide, /en/methodology — there is NO src/app/en/page.tsx and no redirect (verified: find src/app/en -type f + grep for redirects came back empty). So the advertised English alternate URL https://fullstack-eladjak.co.il/en returns 404. Google/AI treat a 404 hreflang target as a broken bidirectional signal and may drop the alternate entirely. Fix: either add src/app/en/page.tsx (an English landing/index), OR add a redirect /en -> /en/claude-code in next.config redirects(), OR change the alternate to point at a real English URL (e.g. /en/claude-code). This is the single most actionable GEO defect.

findings.title: CSP has NO media-src directive — the cinematic video + audio hero will be BLOCKED unless media-src is added first
findings.detail: src/proxy.ts sets `default-src 'self'` and enumerates script/style/img/font/connect but has no media-src. Per CSP, <video>/<audio> fall back to default-src 'self'. A hero served from local /videos/*.mp4 will play (same-origin), BUT (a) any blob: source (common for adaptive/streamed or JS-attached media) is blocked, (b) any CDN/Vercel-blob/Supabase-hosted video is blocked, (c) poster images are covered by img-src (already has https/data/blob, OK). BEFORE shipping the video hero, add `media-src 'self' blob: https:` (scope the https to the actual CDN host). This is a hard pre-flight — the hero will silently fail on prod otherwise. Note proxy matcher already excludes /videos from the nonce pass, so static /videos bytes are served without CSP on that response, but the PAGE that embeds the <video> still enforces this CSP, so media-src governs playback.

findings.title: structured-data.tsx calls await headers() → forces the whole route into DYNAMIC rendering (SSR per request, no static/ISR cache)
findings.detail: src/components/seo/structured-data.tsx reads the per-request CSP nonce via `(await headers()).get('x-nonce')`. Because <StructuredData> is rendered in the root layout on every page, EVERY page is opted into dynamic (SSR) rendering — no full static generation, no CDN HTML caching. That is a deliberate trade for nonce-based CSP, but it (a) raises TTFB vs static, (b) compounds with a heavy video hero (dynamic SSR + large media = slower LCP). Additionally webPage() uses `new Date().toISOString()` for dateModified on every request (layout.tsx line 132), so the JSON-LD dateModified churns per request — harmless but non-deterministic. Consider: render JSON-LD WITHOUT a nonce (JSON-LD needs no nonce if script-src allows it via hash, or accept it as data not executable) to let pages go static; or set an explicit revalidate. At minimum, be aware the site is fully dynamic today — the Lighthouse LCP budget for the video hero must assume SSR TTFB, not static.

findings.title: Video hero CLS + LCP risk: current hero uses min-h-[75dvh] with a priority-preloaded image; a video swap needs fixed aspect-ratio + poster to avoid layout shift and LCP regression
findings.detail: layout.tsx line 137 preloads /images/hero-dev.jpg (`<link rel=preload as=image>`) and hero-section.tsx marks that Image priority+fetchPriority=high — it is the current LCP element. Swapping in a <video>: (1) Do NOT autoplay-download a large mp4 as the LCP path — that tanks LCP and mobile data. Use a lightweight poster image (keep it as the preloaded LCP asset) and only start the video after load/idle. (2) Reserve space with an explicit aspect-ratio / min-height container (the section already has min-h-[75dvh], keep an equivalent fixed box) so the video swap causes ZERO CLS. findings.title: Video hero audio MUST NOT autoplay with sound + MUST honor prefers-reduced-motion — infra is already in place, follow the existing GuideVideo/useReducedMotion patterns
findings.detail: Accessibility infra is strong and reusable: globals.css lines 174-187 kill ALL animation/transition under prefers-reduced-motion (animation-duration .01ms !important globally), and 20+ components already use framer-motion useReducedMotion(). REQUIREMENTS for the cinematic hero: (1) NEVER autoplay audio — browsers block it and it is a WCAG 1.4.2 violation; ship muted-by-default with an explicit unmute control, or decouple audio behind a user gesture. (2) A background/autoplay video MUST be muted + playsInline + loop and MUST be disabled (show poster only) when prefers-reduced-motion:reduce — the global CSS does NOT stop <video> playback, so add an explicit useReducedMotion() gate that renders the poster instead of playing. (3) If audio is a feature, provide captions/transcript for spoken content (WCAG 1.2.2). (4) Follow the existing src/components/agent-guide/GuideVideo.tsx pattern (controls, preload=metadata, playsInline, aria-label) — but for a HERO background video use muted+aria-hidden and keep the text accessible separately.

audits.lens: TECH/ARCHITECTURE — integrating a pinned GSAP ScrollTrigger cinematic section + mutable audio layer into the portfolio (Next.js 16, React 18, next-intl, nonce-CSP)

findings.title: The hero IS a client component — so is the entire homepage body. No RSC-serialization risk exists on this integration path.
findings.detail: src/components/hero/hero-section.tsx is `'use client'` (line 1, uses framer-motion + useTranslations). It is rendered by src/components/sections/home-page-client.tsx which is ALSO `'use client'` and imports every section as a plain client child (HeroSection, StatsBar, SkillsSection, FeaturedProjectsSection, ChatFAQ, CTASection...). The only server boundary is src/app/page.tsx (HomePage, server) → <HomePageClient latestPosts={...}/>, and it already passes ONLY plain serializable fields (slug/frontmatter strings/readingTime — see the explicit comment at page.tsx:46-63). CONSEQUENCE for the safe-live-refactor RSC gotcha: a new pinned GSAP `<section>` dropped INSIDE home-page-client.tsx (as a `'use client'` child) crosses NO server→client boundary — it's client→client. There is zero 'Functions cannot be passed to Client Components' risk on this path, because no new server component is passing props to it. The GSAP section receives nothing non-serializable across an RSC edge. (The only way to reintroduce the risk would be to render the new section directly from the server page.tsx and pass it an object with function/icon/class fields — do NOT do that; keep it a client child of home-page-client.)

findings.title: CSP is nonce + 'strict-dynamic' — GSAP is fully compatible (it injects NO inline scripts), but the audio/video layer WILL be blocked unless you handle media-src.
findings.detail: src/proxy.ts (Next 16's renamed middleware) sets a strict per-request CSP. GSAP + ScrollTrigger are safe: they animate via JS transforms/inline STYLES, never inject <script> tags, so they load as a normal ES chunk through the nonce'd Next bootstrap under 'strict-dynamic' — no CSP change needed for GSAP. THE AUDIO/VIDEO PROBLEM: the CSP has NO `media-src` directive (proxy.ts lines 36-49), so <video>/<audio> fall back to `default-src 'self'`. That means: (a) a scroll-video MP4 and an audio file served from the site's own /videos or /public are ALLOWED (same-origin 'self'); (b) any external/CDN media URL is BLOCKED; (c) a `blob:`-sourced <audio>/<video> (e.g. fetch→createObjectURL, or MediaSource) is BLOCKED because default-src lacks blob:. Note img-src already includes `data: blob:` but that does NOT cover <video>/<audio> — those need media-src. FIX: keep the WebP frames + MP4 + audio file same-origin under /public (then no CSP edit needed), OR if you ever use blob:/MSE or a CDN, add an explicit `media-src 'self' blob:` (and the CDN origin) to the array in proxy.ts. Also: next.config.js sets X-Frame-Options:DENY and proxy sets frame-ancestors 'none' — fine, no iframe involved here.

findings.title: A proven lazy-mount pattern already exists for a heavy visual section (three.js SkillsCanvas) — replicate it exactly for the GSAP section to contain bundle-size + TBT.
findings.detail: src/components/skills-universe/SkillsLazyMount.tsx wraps the heavy 3D canvas in `dynamic(() => import('./SkillsCanvas'), { ssr:false, loading })` and gates the actual mount behind an explicit user click, painting only a static poster <Image> first. Its header comment documents WHY: the 3D bundle (~150KB gz) caused a ~480ms TBT spike and dropped Lighthouse Perf to 52 / LCP >8s. GSAP core+ScrollTrigger is far lighter (~40-70KB gz, no WebGL), but the SAME discipline applies for a homepage above-most-content cinematic section: (1) make the GSAP section its own `'use client'` component; (2) `dynamic(import, { ssr:false })` it so the GSAP bundle + ScrollTrigger.register never touch the SSR HTML or the LCP path; (3) register ScrollTrigger ONLY inside a useEffect/useGSAP (client) — never at module top level (it references window). This keeps GSAP out of the initial JS for crawlers and the hero's LCP, matching the existing architecture rather than fighting it.

findings.title: SSR / JSON-LD are structurally immune to the new section — JSON-LD lives in the server <head>, decoupled from the body.
findings.detail: src/app/layout.tsx (server component) renders 5 <StructuredData> blocks (website/person/localBusiness/faqPage/webPage) directly in <head> (lines 128-132). structured-data.tsx is a server component emitting a plain nonce'd <script type=application/ld+json> via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (lines 106-115) — NOT next/script, so it's always in the initial server HTML. This is fully independent of anything added to the homepage body. IMPORTANT SSR NOTE: home-page-client.tsx documents that below-fold sections were deliberately un-`ssr:false`'d so their content renders into the initial HTML for AI/SEO crawlers (lines 26-30) and ChatFAQ is a static import specifically because it carries the visible FAQ that matches the FAQPage JSON-LD. Therefore: place the GSAP cinematic section so it does NOT displace or wrap the crawler-visible text sections. Best placement = a self-contained decorative band inserted BETWEEN HeroSection and StatsBar (or just after StatsBar), NOT wrapping SkillsSection/FeaturedProjects/ChatFAQ. Because it's `ssr:false`, its own visual content is invisible to crawlers — that's fine for a decorative cinematic stage, but do not put unique indexable copy only inside it.

findings.title: Two animation libraries will coexist (framer-motion v11 + GSAP) — acceptable, but scope GSAP to the one section to avoid double-driving transforms and bundle bloat.
findings.detail: package.json already ships framer-motion@11.18.2 (used by hero + most sections) AND three@0.184 / @react-three/fiber (skills-universe only). Adding gsap is a new top-level dep (not currently installed — confirmed absent from node_modules). Coexistence is fine as long as GSAP is confined to the new section's own DOM subtree: never let GSAP and framer-motion both animate the SAME element's transform (they fight over the style attribute). Since the pinned stage is self-contained, keep all its motion in GSAP and leave the hero's framer-motion untouched. Bundle: import ScrollTrigger from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger' (tree-shakeable) and gate the whole thing behind dynamic ssr:false so it adds ~0 to the shared/first-load chunk. Run `npm run check` (next lint && tsc) after — note this repo uses npm on Windows, NOT bun (per project CLAUDE.md), and the deploy is Vercel/fullstack-eladjak.co.il so follow safe-live-refactor: branch → Vercel PREVIEW deploy → verify Ready before promoting (tsc passing is NOT sufficient proof for anything touching client boundaries or CSP).

findings.title: Pinned ScrollTrigger + RTL + reduced-motion: three concrete runtime gotchas for THIS site.
findings.detail: (1) RTL: <html dir="rtl"> (layout.tsx line 126). ScrollTrigger horizontal scrub math and any `x`/xPercent tweens are direction-sensitive under RTL — vertical pinning is unaffected, but if the cinematic uses horizontal scroll, test the scrub direction in RTL and mirror as needed. (2) prefers-reduced-motion: the site takes this seriously (SkillsLazyMount is gated behind explicit consent partly for this reason; globals/CSS honor reduced-motion). Wrap the ScrollTrigger setup in gsap.matchMedia() with a `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` branch that renders a static frame + no pin/scrub, and default the audio layer to MUTED/off. (3) Pinning inside the existing layout: ClientLayout wraps children in `<div class="pt-16">` + <PageTransition> (framer-motion route transitions). A ScrollTrigger `pin` creates a pin-spacer; ensure the pinned section is a normal-flow block (not inside a transform/overflow-hidden ancestor that would break position:fixed pinning) and call ScrollTrigger.refresh() after fonts/images settle. Also cleanup: kill triggers in the useEffect return (or use useGSAP) so PageTransition route changes don't leak triggers.

opportunities: RECOMMENDED INTEGRATION (exact): Create src/components/sections/cinematic-scroll-section.tsx as a `'use client'` component that (a) registers ScrollTrigger inside useGSAP/useEffect only, (b) builds the pinned stage + WebP-frame/MP4 scroll-scrubbed timeline + an audio-toggle button controlling a same-origin <audio> element with muted default. Then add a thin wrapper src/components/sections/cinematic-lazy-mount.tsx doing `dynamic(() => import('./cinematic-scroll-section'), { ssr:false, loading: <poster> })`, mirroring SkillsLazyMount. Insert <CinematicLazyMount/> in home-page-client.tsx BETWEEN <HeroSection/> and <StatsBar/> (or just after StatsBar). This crosses no RSC boundary, keeps GSAP out of the LCP/SSR/crawler HTML, and cannot touch JSON-LD.

Install: `npm i gsap` (repo uses npm on Windows per CLAUDE.md, not bun). Import tree-shakeably: `import gsap from 'gsap'; import { ScrollTrigger } from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger'; gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)` — the registerPlugin call MUST run client-side (inside the effect), never at module top level (ScrollTrigger touches window/document).

Media hosting decision that avoids ALL CSP edits: put the WebP frame sequence, the MP4 scroll-video, and the audio file under /public (served same-origin). Then `default-src 'self'` already permits them and proxy.ts needs no change. ONLY if you later use blob:/MediaSource or a CDN, add `"media-src 'self' blob:"` (+ the CDN origin) to the CSP array in src/proxy.ts.

Reduced-motion + audio ethics: wrap all ScrollTrigger setup in gsap.matchMedia(); the reduce branch shows a static hero frame with no pin/scrub. Default the audio layer OFF/muted (autoplay-with-sound is blocked by browsers anyway) and expose an explicit toggle with aria-pressed + aria-label — consistent with the site's existing a11y posture (skip-link, IS 5568).

Safe-live-refactor compliance (this is a live Vercel site, fullstack-eladjak.co.il): do the work on a branch, push to a Vercel PREVIEW deploy, verify it's Ready and that CSP does not console-error on the media, run `npm run check` (next lint && tsc --noEmit) — but treat tsc-green as necessary-not-sufficient; the real proof is the preview build + a browser console clean of CSP violations. Only then promote to main.

Cleanup discipline to avoid ScrollTrigger leaks across route changes (PageTransition uses framer-motion route transitions): use the useGSAP hook (or return a cleanup that calls ScrollTrigger.getAll().forEach(t=>t.kill()) scoped to this component) so navigating away doesn't leave dangling pinned triggers. Call ScrollTrigger.refresh() after fonts/images load to fix pin-spacer measurement.
strengths: The homepage body is already an all-client tree (page.tsx server shell → home-page-client.tsx 'use client' → all sections as client children), so adding a client GSAP section introduces NO new server→client prop boundary and therefore NO RSC-serialization crash risk — the exact failure mode safe-live-refactor warns about is structurally absent on this path.

A battle-tested lazy-mount pattern for a heavy visual (three.js SkillsCanvas via dynamic ssr:false + poster + explicit gate) already exists and is documented with its perf rationale — the GSAP section can copy it 1:1 to keep the bundle off the LCP/SSR/crawler path.
JSON-LD is emitted as plain nonce'd server <script> in <head> (layout.tsx + structured-data.tsx), fully decoupled from the body — no body-section change can affect structured data or SEO.

CSP is modern and correct (nonce + strict-dynamic, no unsafe-inline in script-src) and GSAP injects no inline scripts, so GSAP needs zero CSP changes — the only CSP consideration is the media layer, which is trivially solved by hosting media same-origin.

framer-motion v11 and three.js already coexist cleanly with section-scoped usage, so a third, section-scoped GSAP fits the established architecture; npm-on-Windows + Vercel-preview deploy workflow is already the documented norm for safe changes.

highFindings.title: CSP is nonce + 'strict-dynamic' — GSAP is fully compatible (it injects NO inline scripts), but the audio/video layer WILL be blocked unless you handle media-src.
highFindings.detail: src/proxy.ts (Next 16's renamed middleware) sets a strict per-request CSP. GSAP + ScrollTrigger are safe: they animate via JS transforms/inline STYLES, never inject <script> tags, so they load as a normal ES chunk through the nonce'd Next bootstrap under 'strict-dynamic' — no CSP change needed for GSAP. THE AUDIO/VIDEO PROBLEM: the CSP has NO `media-src` directive (proxy.ts lines 36-49), so <video>/<audio> fall back to `default-src 'self'`. That means: (a) a scroll-video MP4 and an audio file served from the site's own /videos or /public are ALLOWED (same-origin 'self'); (b) any external/CDN media URL is BLOCKED; (c) a `blob:`-sourced <audio>/<video> (e.g. fetch→createObjectURL, or MediaSource) is BLOCKED because default-src lacks blob:. Note img-src already includes `data: blob:` but that does NOT cover <video>/<audio> — those need media-src. FIX: keep the WebP frames + MP4 + audio file same-origin under /public (then no CSP edit needed), OR if you ever use blob:/MSE or a CDN, add an explicit `media-src 'self' blob:` (and the CDN origin) to the array in proxy.ts. Also: next.config.js sets X-Frame-Options:DENY and proxy sets frame-ancestors 'none' — fine, no iframe involved here.
